title: Shot
description: Single shot (production/scenes/<SC_ID>/shots/<SH_ID>.yaml): narrative purpose, timing with handles, full camera spec, blocking with eyelines, continuity declarations, required references, and generation flags. The unit /smart-shot produces and every generation pipeline consumes.

scene.description: Scene this shot belongs to; must match the ID's scene number.

order.description: Position within the scene's cut order, 1-based.

narrative.description: Why this shot exists. A shot without a purpose is coverage waste.

purpose.description: What the audience must learn or feel from this shot.

beat.description: Beat label or beat ID this shot lands (e.g. discovery, BT_SC004_02).

emotion.description: Target emotional register of the shot.

timing.description: On-screen duration plus edit handles; generated clips must cover duration + both handles.

duration_seconds.description: Intended on-screen duration in the cut.

handles_before.description: Extra seconds generated before the in-point for the editor.

handles_after.description: Extra seconds generated after the out-point for the editor.

camera.description: Full camera specification; compiled directly into prompt language.

angle.description: Camera position relative to the subject.

height_m.description: Lens height above the floor in meters (eye level ~1.55).

station.description: Optional camera station from the location map this shot is taken from.

distance_m.description: Travel distance in meters for dolly/truck/crane/arc moves.

degrees.description: Sweep in degrees for pan/tilt/arc moves.

blocking.description: Where subjects are, what they do, and where they look. Keys are lowercase character handles (e.g. mara for CHAR_MARA).

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.description: Mark or landmark the character occupies (e.g. beside_bench).

actions.description: Ordered physical actions performed during the shot.

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.description: What the character is looking at (subject, landmark, or handle).

continuity.description: Every shot declares its neighbors, screen direction, and axis; check-continuity.js validates these across cuts.

enters_from.description: Previous shot in the cut; null for the first shot of the scene.

exits_to.description: Next shot in the cut; null for the last shot of the scene.

screen_direction.description: Dominant subject movement/facing direction on screen.

axis_id.description: 180-degree line this shot respects (declared in the scene's continuity-state).

references.description: Reference assets this shot needs; refined per provider by the reference plan.

required.description: Assets that must condition generation (identity, set, hero props).

optional.description: Assets to include if the provider's reference budget allows (style, lighting).

generation.description: Flags telling /generate-keyframes and /generate-clips what to produce.

start_frame_required.description: Generate a start keyframe before the video pass.

end_frame_required.description: Generate an end keyframe (for providers with start/end conditioning).

audio_generation.description: Whether this shot also needs generated audio.

provider.description: Override of the project's default provider for this shot.

dialogue.description: Verbatim dialogue spoken during the shot, if any.
